requirements.requirement: curl package version is locked/held on node1 at its currently installed version
requirements.summary: Baseline captured curl-7.76.1-31.el9 (cmd-43f033514e544041). python3-dnf-plugin-versionlock installed and 'dnf versionlock add curl' applied, with versionlock list confirming curl-0:7.76.1-31.el9.* locked (cmd-eb10229950334047).

requirements.requirement: A system update leaves curl at its current version (lock is effective against real updates)
requirements.summary: repoquery confirmed a newer curl (7.76.1-40.el9_8.7) existed upstream, making the test meaningful; a full dry-run and then a real 'dnf update -y' upgraded 210 packages (including kernel) while curl was excluded from the transaction and remained at 7.76.1-31.el9 afterward (cmd-9e8a6e3c92b84833, cmd-87b519a12dcd4e6d).

Pre-restart boot_id and curl/lock state captured (cmd-3c448f1ad9204c00), reboot acknowledged and node briefly unreachable (cmd-289bc3cfedec46d4), new boot_id with 0-minute uptime confirmed a genuine reboot (cmd-cf15e431860e4e41), and post-restart curl remained 7.76.1-31.el9 with the versionlock entry intact and a fresh dry-run excluding curl (cmd-6c655c5ece884a0c). This also satisfies the provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol for node1.

overall_summary: The executor correctly installed dnf-versionlock and locked curl at its installed version (7.76.1-31.el9) on node1, then convincingly proved the lock's effectiveness by confirming a newer curl was available upstream and running a genuine, full 210-package system update (including the kernel) that left curl untouched. It further followed the mandatory restart-evidence protocol, showing pre-restart healthy state, a real reboot (new boot_id, 0-minute uptime), and post-restart confirmation that both the curl version and the versionlock entry survived. Lifecycle snapshots corroborate the boot-identity change and OS/kernel version bump with no unwanted residue.
limitations: No captured evidence of an attempted targeted 'dnf update curl' actually being blocked with a specific 'excluded by versionlock' style message beyond the aggregate transaction lists and 'Nothing to do' dry-run outputs, though this is a minor evidentiary gap given the multiple corroborating checks.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to task or restart-protocol purposes: installing the versionlock plugin (cmd-eb10229950334047) was required to lock curl; the full 'dnf update -y' upgrading 210 packages including the kernel (cmd-87b519a12dcd4e6d) was a deliberate, bounded test directly demonstrating the task's 'system update leaves it where it is' requirement rather than an unrelated mutation; the reboot (cmd-3c448f1ad9204c00) was the mandatory restart-evidence protocol. Lifecycle diff shows only expected changes (new boot-identity, kernel/OS version bump from the legitimate update, ephemeral systemd-private tmp dirs tied to the new boot, and a small /tmp/reboot.log from the backgrounded shutdown command) — no abandoned files, failed services, or unnecessary mutations were left behind.
